markdown_report:
The best next experiment remains the prespecified **p=0.75 terminal-view allocation**, with checkpoint-linked accounting. At 20% progress, resolving implementation ambiguity remains preferable to adding model complexity; however, without measured gradient variability, this is an allocation hypothesis rather than a variance-optimal design.

Three insights follow from the supplied evidence. First, masked-target discrimination is reasonably strong, but Electronics has weaker lower-tail margins. These training probes cannot establish validation HR@10. Second, item RankMe remains approximately 49–54 while user representations are more concentrated. This does not establish collapse or justify a geometry regularizer. Third, allocation snapshots describe fixed 64/64 branches while definitions describe Bernoulli allocation. Previous behavior therefore cannot be attributed confidently to p=0.75.

Three literature insights guide the experiment. BERT4Rec already uses masked prediction and terminal masking [1]; this proposal changes allocation. Shuffling studies motivate separating order from recency [2], but sensitivity cannot establish current intent. Sampling research distinguishes allocation from gradient interaction [3]; separate branch normalization preserves coefficients 0.5/0.5, rather than changing them to 0.75/0.25.

The framework separates three directions:

| Direction | Controlled variable | Required evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Allocation | Terminal-view probability | Realized counts, target denominators |
| Objective weighting | Branch coefficients | Applied coefficients, branch gradients |
| Context dependence | History perturbations | Paired frozen-model comparisons |

Three atomic ideas remain candidates. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment gives a strength and limitation for each rating.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Audited p=0.75 allocation [1,3] | 2/5/4 | Originality: explicit provenance; potential: controlled foundation; difficulty: local sampler change | Originality: established technique; potential: no measured allocation optimum; difficulty: RNG, accounting and diagnostic integration |
| Fixed 64/64 allocation with terminal loss coefficient 0.75 [1,3] | 2/5/2 | Originality: clean objective contrast; potential: directly tests emphasis; difficulty: scalar change | Originality: standard weighting; potential: may weaken reconstruction; difficulty: still requires faithful integration |
| Recent-versus-older deletion diagnosis [2] | 3/6/4 | Originality: matched controls; potential: tests context dependence; difficulty: frozen-model evaluation | Originality: established perturbations; potential: sensitivity does not identify intent; difficulty: length and position confounding |

Select the first idea. Replace fixed branch counts with 128 seeded Bernoulli draws, preserving branch-specific generators, separate target means, coefficients 0.5/0.5, and absent-branch handling. Expected counts become 96 terminal/32 reconstruction. Expected gradients remain equal only under appropriate count–gradient assumptions: multiple reconstruction targets introduce a random denominator whose correlation with gradients can change the finite-batch expectation [4].

Logical steps: draw branches → construct unchanged views → compute exact losses → update one BERT4Rec → persist checkpoint-linked accounting. Generate definitions from saved configuration and flag disagreements. Retain all four routes, seeds, limits, diagnostic interfaces and pinned evaluator; inference appends MASK and reads the maximum nonpadding index.

Compare available paired user hits using category-stratified bootstrapping [5]. Report inspected checkpoints/configurations; post-selection intervals remain exploratory [6] and, with seed 42 alone, exclude training-run variability [7]. Full-catalog performance is not established by sampled HR [8]. Qualitative feedback supplies no ownership, compatibility or current-need labels.

idea.description: Evaluate one prespecified terminal-view allocation probability, p=0.75, in the corrected BERT4Rec baseline while preserving branch-specific contexts, separate target-mean losses, and coefficients 0.5/0.5. Persist measured allocation and configuration with each category’s single selected checkpoint, and derive diagnostic descriptions from those records. Treat this as a change to the finite-batch gradient estimator and target volume, with neither improved HR@10 nor variance optimality assumed.
idea.motivation: Supplied snapshots report fixed 64/64 allocation whereas metric definitions describe Bernoulli sampling, and another inspiration lacks allocation counters entirely. This prevents reliable attribution. A small allocation intervention with verifiable provenance fits early research progress and tests whether allocating more training views to terminal masked prediction helps under the unchanged host metric. It does not directly infer unresolved needs or establish p=0.75 as optimal. Separate branch normalization retains equal explicit objective coefficients; any expected-gradient equivalence requires assumptions about target counts and gradients. The fixed-allocation loss-weighting idea is the clearer future experiment if the intended question is stronger terminal objective emphasis, while frozen context perturbations address a different diagnostic question.
idea.implementation_notes:
Apply this intervention to the host-supplied corrected baseline; the input does not contain enough backbone or host integration code to provide a faithful standalone train.py replacement. Exact execution remains conditional on the supplied baseline implementation and its recorded configuration. Do not invent missing baseline behavior or inspect other trials.

Keep 128 total generated views per update, drawing independent terminal indicators with probability 0.75. This replaces fixed 64 reconstruction/64 terminal views with expected counts 32 reconstruction/96 terminal views. Preserve independent uniform eligible-user sampling conditional on branch, reconstruction on latest maxlen events with 0.15 MASK-only corruption and fallback, and the supplied terminal prefix-cutoff distribution. Preserve the baseline’s actual cutoff indexing and its documented endpoint probabilities: n=2 selects the endpoint, while n>2 assigns endpoint probability 0.1 and nonterminal probability 0.9/(n-2). Record executable cutoff support, eligibility rules and truncation instead of inferring them from prose. Retain branch-specific generators; do not replace sampled-prefix terminal examples with latest-window terminal masks or claim a shared-window corruption-only comparison.

Preserve RNG stream separation and record the allocation stream explicitly; changing random draw consumption must be disclosed. Use a dedicated deterministic allocation stream keyed by training seed 42, category, epoch and batch, with a recorded unused purpose identifier. Do not consume the existing user, cutoff, mask or negative streams for allocation. Record the complete RNG construction and software versions. Branch counts necessarily change how many conditional draws are consumed; preserving conditional distributions does not imply identical realized examples across schemes.

Compute L=0.5*S_reconstruction/N_reconstruction + 0.5*S_terminal/N_terminal for nonempty branches, with zero contribution from absent branches and no weight redistribution. Preserve summed full-catalog cross-entropy over real items, labels item_id-1, tied real-item embedding weights, no output bias, and exclusion of PAD and MASK from the catalog denominator. Preserve the baseline’s actual optimizer, positional convention, checkpoint selection, validation cadence and stopping behavior. Supplied snapshots describe maxlen 128, hidden width 64, two blocks, two heads, dropout 0.2, Adam learning rate 0.001, weight decay 0, clipping 5, validation every five epochs, patience 20, and earliest maximum category validation HR@10; verify these against the host baseline and record how patience is counted rather than silently overriding it.

Equal branch coefficients do not guarantee identical expected finite-batch gradients. For summed target gradients G, positive target count N and mu=E[G]/E[N], E[G/N]-mu is approximately [mu*Var(N)-Cov(G,N)]/E[N]^2 componentwise under a valid second-order expansion. If E[G|N]=N*mu, normalization is exactly unbiased; random denominators alone do not prove bias. Reconstruction views contain variable numbers of masked targets, so count–gradient correlation may change the expected estimator when their count falls from 64 to about 32. The sign and magnitude are unmeasured. Under the simplifying one-target-per-view, count-independent conditional-mean and independent-view assumptions, both allocations have the same expected gradient apart from empty branches; leading variance factors are about two-thirds for terminal and twice for reconstruction, before count-fluctuation corrections. These are conditional deductions, not observed results or guarantees for Adam. Reconstruction is absent with probability 0.75^128, approximately 1.02e-16; terminal is absent with probability 0.25^128. Record realized absences rather than applying corrections.

Log realized branch examples, valid targets, detached CE sums, exact denominators, applied coefficients, per-target coefficients, coefficient masses, objective contributions, and empty/skipped counts. Coefficient mass is neither loss-value share nor gradient share. Report aggregate CE sums divided by aggregate target counts separately from mean batch objectives. Save selected-epoch and cumulative summaries, their covered training intervals, configuration/source identifiers, baseline identity and selected epoch with the checkpoint. Reload them for diagnosis. Generate definitions from saved protocol fields, validate counts against processed views and updates, and report contradictions explicitly. Do not infer branch identity from diagnostic terminal-position coverage; reconstruction may also supervise the final position. If source or configuration identity cannot be established, report that limitation instead of claiming a verified controlled comparison.

Optional sparse gradient measurements may report branch norms and cosine separately for item embeddings and encoder, with actual loss coefficients and denominators. Covariance requires repeated independent draws and centering; one gradient pair or uncentered alignment cannot establish variance-optimal allocation. Preserve model mode and training RNG, perform no optimizer updates, report counts and zero-gradient handling, and charge all computation to the shared budget. These probes are diagnostic and must not trigger an unplanned adaptive allocation sweep.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), family-specific sample_batch, and all ModelView interfaces. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module; retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Loader output remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. Missing metadata, measurements and unmatched sampler bookkeeping remain unavailable rather than inferred.

Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl routing; DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; maximum 200 epochs; exactly 200 batches per completed epoch; single-GPU execution; and trial-local artifacts. Keep all training, debugging and diagnostic compute within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Train and load exactly one independent model/checkpoint per category, without score fusion, separately fitted auxiliary predictors, independent experts, checkpoint averaging or multi-seed training. Preserve masked-target training without visible shifted-target leakage. Write a matching predictor using the reserved MASK, baseline positional IDs, history truncated to L-1 items, left padding, and maximum nonpadding readout. Preserve checkpoint/predictor-writer architecture, item mapping and configuration consistency.

Host selection remains the unchanged macro validation HR@10 over four categories, each with 200 users and 99 unique negative candidates at evaluation seed 42. Report category values and their unweighted macro average without treating training probes as validation evidence. Retain the baseline checkpoint-selection rule and record every checkpoint evaluation and configuration inspected, including unsuccessful trials. Avoid an unplanned probability sweep or repeated adaptation to this fixed panel. Strong margins, lower rank or recency sensitivity alone establish neither improvement nor shortcut learning. Popularity, latest-item dependence and reconstruction overfitting remain hypotheses rather than measured failures.

If authorized host outputs already contain aligned per-user binary hits for the corrected baseline and proposed predictor on identical candidates, compute d(c,u)=hit_proposed-hit_baseline and Delta=(1/4)*sum_c mean_u d(c,u). Independently resample 200 paired users with replacement within each category for 10,000 replicates using a recorded local analysis seed, such as 42; report Delta, its 2.5th–97.5th percentile interval, category differences, and counts of proposed-only and baseline-only hits. Never access another trial’s files or checkpoints to obtain comparison data, alter the evaluator, or train extra comparison models. If only aggregate HR values are supplied, report the difference without fabricating paired uncertainty. The interval describes user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fitted checkpoints, histories, four categories and fixed candidates, assuming independent users within category. It excludes initialization/minibatch variability, candidate-sampling variability and selection uncertainty. Delta is deterministic for the exact fixed panel. After adaptive checkpoint or configuration selection, the interval is exploratory, even if it excludes zero; preserve the untouched host test for final assessment and do not access it during search.

Keep twenty training-user full-catalog unseen-item recommendations, five per category, separate from pinned host validation. Use only supplied histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions; unavailable ratings, reviews, categories, prices, stores and simulator traits remain unavailable. Histories establish interaction, not ownership, satisfaction, current need or mood. Unsupported qualitative judgments remain unknown. Do not change splits, candidates or evaluator, access test files, fetch external data or pretrained weights, reuse other trials’ checkpoints, or claim sampled HR establishes full-catalog ranking quality.
idea.pseudocode:
CONFIG = {seed: 42, p_terminal: 0.75, batch_size: 128,
          branch_weights: {reconstruction: 0.5, terminal: 0.5}}

for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    baseline = host_corrected_bert4rec(category, CONFIG.seed)
    protocol = capture_actual_baseline_configuration_and_source_identity(baseline)
    protocol.record_allocation_change('fixed 64/64 -> Bernoulli per generated view')
    protocol.record_all_rng_streams_and_unused_allocation_purpose_id()
    counters = initialize_measured_counters()

    for epoch in unchanged_baseline_schedule(max_epochs=200):
        for step in range(200):
            branch_ids = dedicated_seeded_allocation_rng(
                seed=42, category=category, epoch=epoch, step=step,
                purpose=RECORDED_UNUSED_PURPOSE_ID
            ).bernoulli(probability=0.75, size=128)
            # Preserve branch-conditional users, cutoffs, windows and corruption.
            # Terminal targets are hidden; PAD/MASK never become catalog labels.
            batch = baseline.construct_branch_views(branch_ids)
            features = baseline.model.log2feats(batch.sequence)
            loss = differentiable_zero(features)
            for branch in [RECONSTRUCTION, TERMINAL]:
                # Filter by explicit provenance before selecting valid targets.
                S, N = baseline.catalog_ce_sum_and_valid_target_count(
                    features, batch.labels, branch_ids, branch)
                contribution = 0.5 * S / N if N > 0 else differentiable_zero(features)
                loss = loss + contribution
                counters.record(branch, S.detach(), N, contribution.detach(),
                                coefficient=0.5, empty=(N == 0))
            counters.record_realized_view_counts_and_target_provenance(branch_ids, batch)
            baseline.optimizer_step(loss)
        summary = counters.snapshot(epoch)
        assert summary_matches_processed_views_and_updates(summary)
        # Use exactly the baseline cadence, tie policy and stopping semantics.
        baseline.select_checkpoint_with_unchanged_validation_rule(
            additional_payload={protocol, summary})
        record_number_of_checkpoint_evaluations_and_configurations_inspected()

    save_one_selected_checkpoint(category)
    write_predictor_matching_selected_checkpoint(category)

predict(history, candidates):
    sequence = baseline_left_pad(history[-(L-1):] + [MASK])
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
    j = maximum_index_where(sequence != PAD)
    return model.predict_score(features[j], candidates)

run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    metrics = existing_family_specific_probes(train_loader)
    metrics['training_branch_allocation'] = selected_checkpoint.summary
    definitions = definitions_from_saved_protocol(selected_checkpoint.protocol)
    report_protocol_counter_disagreements_explicitly(metrics, definitions)
    return {metrics, metric_definitions: definitions}

# Preserve callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), embedding
# measured metrics and their actual definitions; unavailable evidence stays null.

optional_postprocess_existing_authorized_host_outputs(proposed, baseline):
    require_same_user_ids_categories_and_exact_candidate_lists(proposed, baseline)
    # No reading other trials, evaluator modification, or additional training.
    for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
        d[category] = proposed.hit10[category] - baseline.hit10[category]
        require_exactly_200_aligned_user_pairs(d[category])
        record_category_difference_and_both_discordant_pair_counts(d[category])
    delta = mean([mean(d[c]) for c in FOUR_CATEGORIES])
    rng = local_analysis_rng(seed=42)
    bootstrap = []
    for replicate in range(10000):
        bootstrap.append(mean([
            mean(d[c][rng.choice(200, size=200, replace=True)])
            for c in FOUR_CATEGORIES
        ]))
    report(delta, percentile(bootstrap, [2.5, 97.5]))
    report_conditional_uncertainty_and_post_selection_limitations()
    # If paired outputs are unavailable, omit intervals rather than infer them.

# Host independently evaluates fixed four-category macro validation HR@10.
# This is integration pseudocode; exact reproduction requires the host baseline.

originality.positive: Checkpoint-linked accounting makes the allocation hypothesis interpretable and addresses a concrete contradiction in the supplied evidence.
originality.negative: Terminal masking and altered sampling probabilities are established techniques; this introduces no new modeling principle.

future_potential.positive: A verified allocation baseline supports later controlled studies of objective weighting, gradient variance, finite-batch normalization and context dependence within one network.
future_potential.negative: The chosen probability has no measured optimality justification, and the experiment may leave qualitative relevance failures unresolved.

code_difficulty.positive: The core change remains confined to training-view allocation and checkpoint metadata, with no backbone change.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful RNG handling, branch-context preservation, ratio accounting, restored diagnostics, predictor consistency and optional paired-output analysis require careful integration with the unavailable baseline source.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Uses bidirectional masked-item prediction for sequential recommendation.
Provides the masked prediction foundation and terminal prediction construction retained by this proposal.
limitations: Does not establish p=0.75 as optimal for this task.
Cannot resolve the local implementation’s allocation and diagnostic inconsistencies.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? An Analysis of Datasets for Evaluation of Sequential Recommendations
contributions: Investigates sequential structure through comparisons involving shuffled histories.
limitations: Shuffle sensitivity cannot establish current intent or causal preference evolution.
Its findings do not establish an improvement for the supplied four-category experiment.

related_work.title: PiKE: Adaptive Data Mixing for Multi-Task Learning
contributions: Studies adaptive task sampling informed by gradient interactions.
Motivates distinguishing sampling allocation from objective coefficients and gradient behavior.
limitations: Reported pretraining behavior does not establish corresponding BERT4Rec branch behavior.
No supplied gradient measurements justify adaptive sampling or the selected probability here.

related_work.title: Ratio Estimation in SIMS Analysis
contributions: Discusses finite-sample behavior of ratio estimators.
Provides statistical context for distinguishing an expected normalized gradient from a ratio of expected gradient sums and target counts.
limitations: The application to masked-target gradient normalization is a statistical deduction, not a BERT4Rec result from this work.
Random denominators do not automatically cause bias; numerator–denominator dependence matters.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents bootstrap confidence intervals and paired resampling.
Supports preserving within-user pairing when comparing outcomes from two predictors.
limitations: The proposed category-stratified macro bootstrap is an application of the paired-bootstrap principle.
Aggregate HR values cannot reconstruct paired outcomes, and selected-model bootstrapping does not correct adaptive selection.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains overfitting of model-selection criteria and resulting performance-evaluation bias.
Motivates recording the search and checkpoint-selection process and preserving an untouched final assessment.
limitations: Does not quantify selection optimism for this particular search.
Existing adaptively reused validation outputs cannot supply an independent assessment merely through postprocessing.

related_work.title: Accounting for Variance in Machine Learning Benchmarks
contributions: Distinguishes sources of variability in machine-learning benchmark comparisons.
Motivates separating user-sampling uncertainty from training-run and other benchmark variability.
limitations: A single training seed cannot estimate initialization or minibatch variability.
The required single-seed experiment supports conclusions conditional on its fitted checkpoints.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes limitations of sampled recommendation metrics.
Shows why sampled-candidate comparisons need not preserve full-catalog model rankings.
limitations: Does not replace the mandated pinned evaluator.
User bootstrapping with fixed candidate lists does not measure negative-candidate sampling uncertainty.
